Macrons

Consonantal i

Conversation, family & daily routines

well done phrase

praise

also good job, you carried that well

classical

Traupman 322
Liv. II 12, 14
Cic. Att. XII 6, 3
Verg. Aen. IX 641: macte novā virtūte, puer

Macte virtūte!

The final e of macte is short.

Examples

  • Bene portāvistī.

    You carried that well.composed

  • Bene factum!

    Well done!Libellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium

  • Pulchrē, bene, rēctē!

    praise for a finished result: Dad over the pies, in Horace’s words (Ars 428)Libellus IV, Diēs Grātulātiōnis

  • Pater puerum Rōmānōrum illud «Macte virtūte!» docuerat; quod igitur Baba Bulgaricē dīcit, puer ipse sibi Latīnē.

    Dad had taught the boy the Roman “Macte virtūte!”; so what Baba says in Bulgarian, the boy says to himself in Latin.Libellus VII, Diēs ūnus Osoitsae

  • Cui pater «Rēctē factum!» inquit.

    Dad said to him, “Well done!”Libellus I, Iter in Lūsitāniam

Other words

  • Bene factum!

    also used · classical · Traupman 99

    Said by Dad in Libellus V.

  • Rēctē factum!

    also used · modern · Traupman 101

  • Pulchrē, bene, rēctē! — praise for a finished result

    also used · classical · Hor. Ars 428

    Dad over the pies in Libellus IV.

  • Tū decus omne tuīs. — you are the pride of your family

    also used · classical · Verg. Ecl. 5, 34

    Said to the cook.

See also job.
